description: Rajas con Crema is a beloved Mexican comfort food, featuring tender strips of roasted poblano peppers bathed in a rich, creamy sauce. This vegetarian delight offers a perfect balance of smoky heat and savory creaminess, making it an incredibly versatile dish. It's a taste of home, perfect as a side or a hearty filling for tacos and quesadillas.

ingredients.notes: roasted, peeled, seeded, and cut into strips

instructions.title: Roast the Poblano Peppers
instructions.text: Place poblano peppers directly over an open flame (gas burner) or under a broiler, turning frequently, until the skin is charred and blistered all over. This will take about 8-10 minutes.

instructions.title: Peel and Slice Peppers
instructions.text: Immediately transfer the charred peppers to a bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel. Let them steam for 10-15 minutes. Once cooled, peel off the skin, remove the stem and seeds, and cut the flesh into thin strips (rajas).

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or comal over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced white onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine with Peppers and Corn
instructions.text: Add the prepared poblano strips (rajas) and corn kernels to the skillet with the onion and garlic. Sauté for 3-5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Simmer
instructions.text: Stir in the Crema Mexicana (or sour cream) and whole milk. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally. If using, add the crumbled queso fresco or shredded Oaxaca cheese and stir until melted and incorporated.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the Rajas con Crema with salt to taste. Continue to simmer for another 2-3 minutes until the sauce has slightly thickened and all ingredients are heated through. Serve hot.

tips: For the best smoky flavor, always char your poblanos directly over an open flame or under a hot broiler until fully blistered.
If Crema Mexicana is unavailable, a good quality full-fat sour cream thinned slightly with a touch of milk works well as a substitute.
Rajas con Crema is incredibly versatile; enjoy it as a side dish, a filling for tacos or quesadillas, or even stirred into scrambled eggs for breakfast.
